prompt:
Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1458
Claimant:
Steve Kelly
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
14 Nov 2024
First notice of loss came in by phone from the driver, who reported a low-speed head-on collision at a residential
intersection. The drievr is named on the policy, and I confirmed the vehicle and coverage details before assigning the
file.
25 Nov 2024
Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney, and took a recorded statement describing the impact
and the seat position at the time. The account was consistent with the damage reported at intake.
30 Nov 2024
The responding officer's report and two witnesses at the scene confirm the claimant was in the vehicle when it was
struck. No independent witness saw the moment of impact itself.
21 Jan 2025
Reviewed the photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm the location of the front-end damage and the airbag
status, but it is unclear whether all of the visible damage came from this single impact.
31 Mar 2025
The claimant reported neck and back pain and was seen at urgent care. The reported injury is plausible for a collision
of this type, and no prior injury to the same body area appears in the records available to me.
11 Apr 2025
Received a call from a neighbor who believes the vehicle was already damaged some weeks before the claimed loss.
The information is secondhand, and I have not yet been able to verify it with the claimant or other sources.
15 Apr 2025
Checked the vehicle history and prior claims. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, though the search does
not cover unreported repairs. I am requesting the repair estimates and the shop's intake photos to compare.
30 Apr 2025
Followed up with the claimant, who again gave the same account of the collision and the sequence of events as in
every prior contact. Treatment has followed a usual course, with phsyical therapy visits tapering off as symptoms
improved.
23 May 2025
Reviewing the file with the treatment records, the photos, and the repair estimates in hand. The injury appears
consistent with the mechanics of the collision, and the open question is the extent of vehicle damage attributable to
this impact. Next step is to obtain an independent estimate and the neighbor's contact details for a follow-up
statement.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
